2026-09-01T12:39:02.6458374Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6458759Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6459082Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6459570Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6459964Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6460461Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6462004Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6463898Z >
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6466173Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6468558Z >
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6469349Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6470102Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6470291Z ### How to Use
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6470530Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6471188Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6471953Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6472132Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6472851Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6473578Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6474190Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6474400Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6474659Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6475196Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6475738Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6476529Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6478499Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6479811Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6480042Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6480726Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6481604Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6482374Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6483098Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6483304Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6483636Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6484850Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6485441Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6486309Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6487017Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6487225Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6487499Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6487918Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6489691Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6491608Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6491795Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6578289Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6579739Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6580604Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6580957Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6581523Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6583488Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6586281Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6586868Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6588313Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6589819Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6591582Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6592060Z ```bash
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6594529Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6595545Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6596275Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6596719Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6597137Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6598319Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6598904Z ```
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6599112Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6599341Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6600186Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6620031Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6621679Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6628210Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6632911Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6633532Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6635201Z ### Notes
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6635556Z 
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6637129Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6643675Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6645065Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6646327Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6648005Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6649661Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6651749Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-01T12:39:02.6653144Z </mcp-clis>
